headline: Shaking muscles, a teacher's first year and a hungry fox
teaser: Why does your body shake on a cold morning? What did a new teacher drop in her first lesson? And who took the bread from the tent?

articles.title: Why Do We Shiver When We Are Cold?
articles.dek: Your body shakes on cold days. It is not a mistake. It is a clever plan!
paras: It is a cold winter morning. You are waiting for the school bus, and the wind is stronger than yesterday. Suddenly, your body starts to shake. Your teeth make a funny noise too. Why does this happen? Let's find out.

Your body likes to stay at about 37 degrees. This is much warmer than the air on most winter days. A small part of your brain checks your temperature all the time. It works like the heating in a house. When your skin gets colder, your brain notices very quickly.

Then your brain sends a message to your muscles. It tells them to get tight and then loose again, many times every second. This is shivering. Moving muscles make heat. So when you shiver, your body gets warmer. Shivering makes heat faster than walking slowly.

Have you ever had goosebumps? They come from the cold too. Tiny muscles in your skin pull your hairs up. In animals with thick fur, this keeps warm air near the skin. But it doesn't help people much. Our hair is shorter and thinner than an animal's fur.

Shivering is useful, but it uses a lot of energy. Your body burns food to make the heat. So you may feel hungrier after a long time in the cold. Running or jumping is a better way to warm up. It is more fun too!

So what can you do on a cold day? Wear a hat, a warm coat and a glove on each hand. Two thin jumpers are often warmer than one thick jumper, because there is warm air between them. If you start to shiver, go somewhere warmer. And if someone shivers for a long time and feels confused, they need a doctor.

articles.title: My First Year as a Teacher
articles.dek: Our new science teacher answers questions about her very first school.
paras: Ms Novak is the new science teacher at Lakeside School. Last week, two students from the school magazine, Ben and Yuki, asked her about her first year as a teacher.

Ben: Where did you teach first? Ms Novak: At a small school in a village near the mountains. There were only eighty students. I didn't know anyone there, and I didn't have a car. So I went to school by bike every day, even in the rain!

Yuki: Did you feel nervous on your first day? Ms Novak: Yes, I did! I didn't sleep well the night before. In my first lesson, I dropped a box of test tubes. Luckily, they didn't break. The students laughed, and then I laughed too. After that, I felt much better.

Ben: What did you find difficult? Ms Novak: Remembering names! I had six classes, so I didn't learn all the names quickly. Once, I called a boy Tom for two weeks. His name was Sam! He didn't tell me, because he was very shy.

Yuki: Did your students like science? Ms Novak: Not at first. Many of them didn't enjoy it, because the lessons were only from the book. So I changed things. We grew plants, made paper rockets and went outside to look at insects. Soon, science was their favourite subject.

Ben: Why did you come to Lakeside School? Ms Novak: My family moved to this town last summer. I didn't want to leave my old school, but I'm happy here. Everyone is friendly, and the science lab is great.

Yuki: Last question. Did you always want to be a teacher? Ms Novak: No, I didn't! When I was your age, I wanted to be a pilot. But I liked science more than planes in the end. Yuki: Thank you, Ms Novak!

articles.title: The Fox at the Campsite
articles.dek: Everyone was busy by the fire. Then someone hungry came to visit.
paras: Last August, Leila and her family went camping by a lake. Her little brother, Omar, was eight. It was his first time in a tent, and he was very excited.

On the first evening, the sun was going down when they finished dinner. Dad was washing the plates while Mum was looking at the map for the next day. Leila and Omar were sitting by the fire. They were telling funny stories, and nobody was watching the food bag.

Then Omar heard a noise behind the tent. "What's that?" he whispered. Leila turned around. A small red fox was standing next to the food bag! While they were watching, it put its nose inside. Then it ran into the trees with something in its mouth.

"Our sausages!" shouted Omar. Dad laughed. "No, look. It took the bread." But there was a bigger problem. The bread was for breakfast, and the nearest shop was ten kilometres away. The fox also tore the bag, and the milk was all over the grass.

The next morning, Leila woke up early. While the others were sleeping, she walked down to the lake. A man was fishing there. His name was Mr Hughes, and he worked at the campsite. Leila told him about the fox.

"That fox is always hungry!" he said with a smile. "Keep your food in the car at night." Then he gave her six eggs and some bread from the campsite café. When Leila got back, Mum was making a new fire. They all had a great breakfast together.
That night, the food was in the car. While Omar was falling asleep, he heard a small noise outside the tent. He smiled. "Sorry, fox," he said quietly. "No bread for you tonight!"

items.why: You takes were: What were you doing?

kps.fact: Leila's family went camping by a lake last August.
While the family was busy, a fox came and took the bread.
The nearest shop was ten kilometres away.
kps.q: How far was the nearest shop?

kps.fact: Mr Hughes gave Leila six eggs and some bread.
On the second night, the food was in the car.
kps.q: Where was the food on the second night?

mindmap.question: What happened on the camping trip?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the story.
summary.model: While the family was busy, a fox took their bread, so they had no breakfast. But a kind man at the campsite helped them.

options.t: While the family was busy by the fire, a fox took their food.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 2 and 3.
options.evidence: A small red fox was standing next to the food bag!

options.t: A man at the campsite gave Leila food for breakfast.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 5 and 6.
options.evidence: Then he gave her six eggs and some bread from the campsite café.

options.t: The next night, the family kept their food in the car.
options.why: This is how the story ends.
options.evidence: That night, the food was in the car.

options.t: Dad was washing the plates after dinner.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: Dad was washing the plates while Mum was looking at the map for the next day.

options.t: The family caught a big fish in the lake.
The fox took the family's sausages.

speak.p: Would you like to go camping? Why or why not? What would you take with you?
speak.hint: I'd like to … because … / I would take …

write.p: Look at this sentence: "We were sitting by the fire when we heard a strange noise." Write the story. Write 35 words or more.
steps: Say where you were and who was with you.
